text: Code refactoring means improving the internal structure of code without changing what it does. The main goal is to make code easier to read, understand, and maintain. Common changes include renaming variables for clarity, breaking long functions into smaller ones, and removing duplicate code. Refactoring does not add new features or fix bugs—it simply cleans up the design. Over time, without refactoring, code becomes messy and harder to work with, building up what developers call technical debt. Regularly refactoring helps control this debt, keeping the codebase healthy and the team more productive.
